finalists.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
finalists.why: Strong evidence from histopathology and immunohistochemistry, including dermal tumor infiltration and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.

finalists.label: Breast cancer
finalists.why: Positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, as well as the presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor-positive apocrine glands.

finalists.label: Adenocarcinoma of Unknown Primary
finalists.why: Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, as well as positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.

frontier_selector.why: The champion, Hidradenocarcinoma, is chosen due to its strong evidence from histopathology and immunohistochemistry, including dermal tumor infiltration and positive staining for specific markers, which is more specific to this diagnosis than the runner-up, Breast cancer.

support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors
contradict_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
